note:
PROVE 2026-10-15. The rule is proved in the FIXED-POINT ALGEBRA: V = functions on the 2^N specialisation points u = w_M, pointwise product. The specialised weight functions are a basis of V (triangularity + nonzero root-product diagonal), so structure constants exist and are unique; they vanish unless nu >= lambda and nu >= mu, satisfy a well-founded recursion, have closed root-product form at the extremal labels, and admit a closed 2^N-term localisation formula via Motegi's own explicit matrix inverse. TWO MEASURED NEGATIVES bound what a combinatorial rule could be: (a) the identity does NOT lift to functions of u (0/16 pairs at N=n=2); (b) the structure constants are NOT Laurent polynomials, and the failure locus is SHARP: they are Laurent if and only if |nu| - max(|lambda|,|mu|) <= 1, a criterion matching 225/225 support-bound triples at N=2 and N=3 with zero errors either way. Smallest witness c^{(1,2)}_{empty,empty} at N=2, a simple pole on w1 w2 = 1, the root hyperplane of t_1+t_2 in Delta^+(C_2). So no puzzle-style monomial-weight count can exist at cardinality jump >= 2 in this normalisation (and a diagonal rescaling makes it worse, 29/30 -> 4/30), while on the jump <= 1 stratum a puzzle rule remains open. The brief's own fork is therefore resolved on the 'wrong normalisation' side, NOT against the G_m formal group. CENSUS GATE at position zero did three things: it retired the brief's pre-registered row-4 falsifier as unusable (R(u_i,u_j^{-1}) IS a type-A R-matrix at an inverted argument, so the u_j u_k coupling does not require a boundary piece); it located the real separation in row 3 (q free vs the q=0 five-vertex puzzle); and it found the brief's table carrying ONE row for TWO groups -- S_n on u (which MATCHES type A) versus W(X_N) of rank N on w (which does not, and which is the group whose inversion/ascent sets write the diagonal evaluation). Ninth instance of the one-coordinate-match instrument.

PROVE 2026-10-16 (Q488/Q492). The pre-registered gate CLOSED Q492 NEGATIVELY in under 30 minutes: Motegi's boundary-degeneration count is n-s, not n-r; n is gauge (stability); and the invariant residue |M|-|I| is a row-vs-column gap while the jump is a column-vs-column gap -- cardinality gaps in DIFFERENT SLOTS of the same matrix, a one-coordinate match. Session then went to the same object and PROVED one direction of Q484's measured criterion. MECHANISM: the candidate pole divisors (read off Motegi's diagonal root product) fall into four families, and they split by whether the divisor is a COLLISION of two of the 2^N specialisation points. w_a=1 (padding collision via stability), w_a=-1 (via Atilde(-w)=Atilde(w)) and w_a=w_b (literal collision) all admit a collapse Atilde_{M,I}|_D = Atilde_{tau M,I}|_D with tau(M)<M, which forces the recursion's numerator to vanish to matching order => NO POLE EVER, for all triples. The long-root divisors w_a w_b = 1 are NOT collisions (w_a^{-1} is not among the w_c or the padding 1's) and that asymmetry is the whole theorem. There a pole is created iff some pair deletion nu\{a,b} stays above both lambda and mu, which is EXACTLY jump >= 2 by a two-line cardinality argument -- and that is where the puzzling max() in the criterion comes from. Hence jump <= 1 => Laurent, PROVED. The mechanism predicts the exact pole DIVISOR, not just Laurent-ness: 20/20 at N=2 and 115/115 at N=3. Both pre-registered plants fire (P1 moves the pole to w_a^2=q, P2 to w_a w_b=q). Two precisely-stated gaps remain: the q-shifted family (verified, not proved) and the non-vanishing converse. NOTE on method: the jump criterion and a rival 'uncovered' criterion |nu\(lambda u mu)|<=1 BOTH predict 176/195 at N=3 but disagree on 12 triples -- the matching COUNT was not a matching SET, and computing the 12 decided it for the jump criterion 7/7. Q484's conj:locus stands.

PROVE 2026-10-16 c2 (gap nonvanishing). The Task-0 gate returned a FOURTH outcome, none of the three pre-registered: Rick's q=0 measurement reproduces and is VACUOUS on the triples it was aimed at, because ord_q(c) = 1 in 25/25 pole records, so the non-Laurent constants are exactly the ones that VANISH at q=0 -- and zero is Laurent. The brief's instruction to amend the paper with a q-genericity hypothesis is withdrawn: q is an indeterminate in F = C(q)(w), so 'has a pole' is already generic in q and specialisation does not commute with it. Asking WHERE that factor of q lives produced the mechanism. THEOREM A: on a long-root divisor every factor of Motegi's branching formula with one leg in {a,b} is paired with its own image under w_a <-> w_b, so the branch index, the complement and L all drop out and Atilde_{M,I} = rho Atilde_{M-ab,I} mod (w_a w_b - 1) with rho = (1-q)^2/((1-q w_a^2)(1-q w_a^{-2})) universal. A long-root divisor IS a collapse -- twisted by a scalar; the rows collide projectively even though the points do not. The whole pole phenomenon is then measured by rho - 1 = q(w_a - w_a^{-1})^2/(...), which (i) is nonzero, so poles exist, (ii) carries exactly one factor of q, PREDICTING ord_q(residue) = 1 before it was checked, and (iii) equals 0 at q = 0, which DERIVES Rick's M2 via collision-divisors-no-pole. Four theorems follow: the '<=' half of exact-pole-divisor (was a conjecture); every long-root pole is simple; the created pole is real with a closed-form residue on the minimal stratum (19/19 at N=3, conditional on the measured nonvanH); and an exact residue recursion. SCOPE REPORTED HONESTLY: the minimal stratum is 1/1, 12/13, 99/127, 690/1136, 4335/9748 of the jump>=2 triples at N=2..6 -- DECREASING with N -- so this is a partial closure and gap-propagation is the bulk, not an edge case. Type B gets its first numbers: the collapse holds there too, same rho, 48/48.

Theorem A: c^nu_{lambda,mu} != 0 implies nu >= lambda and nu >= mu, by well-founded induction along >= using only triangularity and Delta_nu != 0. This is the type B/C analogue of the classical nu contains lambda, mu. Measured 64/64 at N=2 and 512/512 at N=3, type C.

children.statement: HYPOTHESIS (2026-10-16 wake): the determinant/Pfaffian dichotomy is the SAME stratification as Q484's jump |nu|-max(|lambda|,|mu|), via Motegi's count of spectral parameters specialised to 1.
children.reason: The count is n-s, not n-r (Motegi states the distinction himself, L2790: 'r specifies the label cardinality, whereas s specifies the number of selected w-variables'). The wake note's n-r was read off the s=r stratum, where the two agree, and carried off it. Worse, n is a GAUGE parameter annihilated by stability eq:typeC-stability-s-ge-r, so n-r takes every value >=0 on the witness. The gauge-invariant residue s-r = |M|-|I| is a cardinality gap between an EVALUATION POINT and a BASIS LABEL (a row/column pair of Atilde), whereas the jump is a gap among THREE BASIS LABELS. Gaps in different slots of the same matrix: a one-coordinate match (both are cardinality gaps between increasing sequences in [N]; both vanish on M=I). Closed in under 30 min by the pre-registered gate. DREAM 2026-10-16 corroboration, from a route sharing NOTHING with the above: BROWSE 2026-10-16 (02:55, three hours before this gate ran) independently retired the same hypothesis as MALFORMED. (i) The closed form is classified by WHICH K-matrix and is >=4-valued with an uncomputed cell, not binary (ordinary DW generic-elliptic = determinant; DW at free-fermion = factorized product; diagonal/U-turn K = determinant, Tsuchiya JMP 39 (1998) 5946-5951; antidiagonal OS at free-fermion = Pfaffian, 1806.00933 Thms 4.2/4.4; upper-triangular 2610.15344 eq (2.14) = sign-free symmetrization, measured NOT a determinant and NOT a Pfaffian; antidiagonal at generic elliptic = UNCOMPUTED). The wake hypothesis matched the ANTIDIAGONAL K against the UPPER-TRIANGULAR K on the single word 'non-diagonal' -- two different matrices. (ii) The word 'locus' presupposes a connected family and Motegi denies one (1806.00933, verbatim: 'It seems that it is hard or maybe impossible to extract the off-diagonal K-matrix from the general full K-matrices of elliptic integrable models'); his K is a CONSTANT antidiagonal implementing the Felder-Schorr antiperiodic BC, not a deformation of a diagonal K. (iii) MEASURED, not read: putting a knob c on the K off-diagonal and contracting the lattice gives Z_{n,m} exactly homogeneous of degree m in c (ratios 2,4,8,4 = 2^m), vanishing identically at c=0, because the only spin-flipping weight in the model is <1|K|0>. So the diagonal boundary ANNIHILATES this partition function rather than degenerating it, and Tsuchiya's determinant is a DIFFERENT partition function, not a limit of this one -- controls 26/26 against direct lattice contraction, 75/75 and 45/45 against Motegi's own Properties (3)/(4), three negative controls firing and one informatively spared at n=m where prod_{j=m+1}^n (Bu-A) is an empty product. Both routes discharged the failure mode the 10-15 dream pre-registered against itself. REPLACEMENT: the dichotomy is indexed by ROW DOUBLING (a row paired with its own reflection), not by the boundary, and the divisor classification above says poles live ONLY on w_a w_b = 1, i.e. w_b = w_a^{-1} -- the reflection-pairing locus -- while the never-poled divisors are the FIXED POINTS of that same involution (w_a = +-1) and a non-reflecting collision (w_a = w_b). That is Q495, stated with four pre-registered failure modes (the first being SLOT: the transition matrix's w vs a Fredholm kernel's arguments) in memory/connections/2026-10-16-dream-a-pfaffian-is-a-doubled-row.md. Q495 is a conjecture with no computation behind it.

children.statement: THEOREM. Call D a collision divisor if some tau with tau(M)<M satisfies Atilde_{M,I}|_D = Atilde_{tau M,I}|_D for all I. Then ord_D c^nu_{lambda,mu} >= 0 for ALL triples -- unconditionally, no jump hypothesis. The divisors w_a=1 (padding collision, via u-symmetry + stability), w_a=w_b (literal point collision), and w_a=-1 (via the symmetry Atilde(-w)=Atilde(w), sign exponent n(n+1)+2nN-2r = 0 mod 2) are all collision divisors. Proof: evaluate the defining identity at M=tau(nu); since tau(nu)<nu, the kappa-sum there is a sub-sum of the recursion's, so the numerator vanishes to matching order. ANSWERS the pre-registered u=-1 control: the u=-1 branch is NON-trivial -- a genuine second collision divisor with the same collapse map -- unlike the q=-1 collapse of 10-15.

Proof: by motegi-branching-formula every surviving K satisfies K>=I, and if some surviving K missed {a,b} then K subset M\{a,b} would witness M\{a,b} >= I by Motegi's top-r criterion; so every surviving term carries the factor. children.statement: LEMMA. For nu>=lambda, nu>=mu: there exists a pair {a,b} subset nu with nu\{a,b} >= lambda and nu\{a,b} >= mu  <=>  |nu| - max(|lambda|,|mu|) >= 2. Forward by cardinality; backward by deleting the two SMALLEST elements of nu, which leaves the top max(|lambda|,|mu|) elements untouched because Motegi's order compares only the top r. This is WHERE THE max COMES FROM: a pole needs the deleted pair to dominate BOTH lambda and mu, an 'and' whose negation is the 'or' that makes the criterion read min(|nu|-|lambda|,|nu|-|mu|)<=1.
children.approach: Pure combinatorics on Motegi's shifted-dominance order: forward by cardinality, backward by deleting the two SMALLEST elements of nu, which leaves the compared top-r window untouched.

children.statement: THEOREM (the 'if' half of Q484's conj:locus, previously only measured). If |nu|-max(|lambda|,|mu|) <= 1 then c^nu_{lambda,mu} has no pole on any long-root divisor w_a w_b = 1; with collision-divisors-no-pole and q-family-row-minimality it is a Laurent polynomial. Proof: induction along a linear extension. The hypothesis is INHERITED -- every kappa in the recursion has |kappa| <= |nu| <= max+1, so jump is monotone in |nu| along Motegi's order and no pole can be created below nu and inherited. Each term is handled by Lemma A: |nu|-2 < max(|lambda|,|mu|) <= |kappa| forces nu\{a,b} not>= kappa.

A counter-measurement can refute an inference drawn from a claim without refuting the claim. Also measured: every long-root pole is simple (mult 1 in 25/25), and ord_q(residue) = ord_q(c) = 1. Correction to the brief: it asserted conj:divisor 'predicts 19 poles at N=3'; the figure 19 appears neither in the paper nor in the measurement -- the truth is 13 triples / 25 (triple,divisor) records, matching Q488's own verification section.
children.approach: Form c^nu as a rational function over QQ(q)(w) first, then (a) factor its denominator for the GENERIC pole census and (b) divide by q^{ord_q} before setting q=0, so that a constant which vanishes at q=0 is not silently scored as Laurent.

children.statement: THEOREM A. For a<b with {a,b} subset M and M' = M\{a,b}: Atilde_{M,I} = rho * Atilde_{M',I} mod (w_a w_b - 1) for EVERY I, with rho = (1-q)^2/((1-q w_a^2)(1-q w_a^{-2})) independent of M, of I, of the branch index K, and of N. Proof: in Motegi's branching formula the label I occurs only inside Phi_{K,I} = W_{N,r}(w_K|w|I)/prod(1-q w_k^{-1} w_k') * prod(1-w_k^{-1} w_k'^{-1}), which depends on (K,I) alone; the remaining factors Psi depend on (K,L,M^c) alone. Terms with K meeting {a,b} vanish on H by long-root-order-lemma, so the surviving index set is exactly that of M'. On H, w_b = w_a^{-1}, and EVERY factor with ONE leg in {a,b} is accompanied by its own image under w_a <-> w_b, so four ratios collapse to 1: the K-dependence (h(k) = 1), the L-dependence (Pi_4 against Pi_5), the M^c-dependence (Pi_5 against Pi_1), and (1-q w_a^{-1} w_b^{-1}) = (1-q) = (1-q w_a w_b). What survives is the one factor with BOTH legs in {a,b}, against the leading (1-q)^{|L|}. Verified independently on the brute-force S_n engine (which never uses the branching formula): 48/48 at N=3 type C and 48/48 type B over a 12-item non-degenerate domain; plant rho -> rho(1+q) fails 12/12 and plant rho -> 1 (the untwisted/collision reading) fails 12/12, on exactly that domain and nowhere else. SO: a long-root divisor IS a collapse, twisted by a scalar. Q488's 'the long-root divisors are not collision divisors ... this is the whole asymmetry' has the right conclusion and an incomplete reason -- the specialisation POINTS do not collide, but the ROWS do, projectively.
children.approach: Separate the branching formula into an I-carrying slot and an I-free slot, then restrict the slot ratio to w_b = w_a^{-1} and observe that the inversion involution pairs each mixed factor with itself.

children.statement: rho - 1 = q (w_a - w_a^{-1})^2 / ((1-q w_a^2)(1-q w_a^{-2})), from (1-q)^2 - (1-q w_a^2)(1-q w_a^{-2}) = q(w_a^2 - 2 + w_a^{-2}). Three consequences. (i) rho != 1, and since basis elements collapse with multiplier rho while their pointwise PRODUCTS collapse with rho^2, the Laurent property must fail: the discrepancy is rho(rho-1) Atilde_{M',lam} Atilde_{M',mu}. (ii) The numerator carries EXACTLY ONE factor of q, so every long-root residue has ord_q = 1 -- derived from the branching formula and only then matched against 25/25 pole records, a prediction and not a fit. (iii) rho|_{q=0} = 1, so at q=0 the twist trivialises and the long-root divisor BECOMES a collision divisor, whereupon collision-divisors-no-pole forbids a pole: this DERIVES q0-gate-vacuous rather than merely accommodating it. The other zero locus of rho-1 is w_a^2 = 1, a short-root divisor whose intersection with H_ab has codimension 2 and is therefore invisible to a divisor statement -- so the exceptional locus in q is exactly {0} (and q = infinity).
children.approach: One line of algebra on the surviving factor, then read its zero locus as a subset of the q-line and separate the codimension-2 part.

children.statement: THEOREM. The '<=' half of exact-pole-divisor, previously only conjectured. Say kappa BRACKETS (a,b) if {a,b} subset kappa and kappa\{a,b} >= lambda and >= mu. If NO kappa with nu >= kappa >= lambda, kappa >= mu brackets (a,b), then ord_{H_ab} c^nu >= 0. Proof by induction along a linear extension. The hypothesis is inherited downward by transitivity of Motegi's order. If {a,b} not subset nu then ord_H Atilde_{nu,nu} = 0 and every term of the recursion is regular. If {a,b} subset nu, the hypothesis at kappa = nu gives nu' = nu\{a,b} not>= lambda (wlog), so long-root-order-lemma makes ord_H Atilde_{nu,lambda} >= 1; and for every contributing kappa we have kappa >= lambda, so nu' >= kappa would give nu' >= lambda by TRANSITIVITY -- contradiction -- hence nu' not>= kappa and ord_H Atilde_{nu,kappa} >= 1 as well. Both terms beat ord_H Atilde_{nu,nu} = 1. This strictly generalises laurent-criterion-if-direction, which is the case where jump-equals-pair-deletion makes the hypothesis hold for every pair at once; the point of the generalisation is that it is available DIVISOR BY DIVISOR, which is what the minimality argument of created-pole-residue consumes.
children.approach: Run Q488's thm:main induction one divisor at a time instead of all divisors at once, and get the no-propagation clause from transitivity of the order rather than from cardinality.

children.statement: THEOREM. ord_{H_ab} c^nu_{lam mu} >= -1 for all triples and all a<b: every long-root pole is SIMPLE. Proved from the OBSTRUCTION IDENTITY, got by applying the collapse to the defining relation rather than to the triangular recursion: with u_{M,I} := (Atilde_{M,I} - rho Atilde_{M',I})/t in the local ring (t = w_a w_b - 1), subtracting rho times the relation at M' from the relation at M gives, for every M containing {a,b}, sum_nu c^nu u_{M,nu} = rho(rho-1) Atilde_{M',lam} Atilde_{M',mu}/t + (terms in the local ring). Taking M = nu, triangularity gives Atilde_{nu',nu} = 0, so u_{nu,nu} = Atilde_{nu,nu}/t is a UNIT; solving for c^nu and inducting gives ord >= -1. Measured: multiplicity 1 in 25/25 pole records at N=3. COROLLARY (the residue recursion): the residues gamma_nu = (t c^nu)|_H satisfy sum_nu gamma_nu u_{M,nu}|_H = rho(rho-1) Atilde_{M',lam}|_H Atilde_{M',mu}|_H -- which is what makes gap-propagation a statement about non-cancellation between two WRITTEN-DOWN terms instead of about branch terms.
children.approach: Apply the twisted collapse to eq:star rather than to eq:rec, so that pole propagation is bookkept by the kernel condition on the leading polar vector instead of being chased term by term.

children.statement: Depends on longroot-twisted-collapse (same registry, sibling node) for u_{M,I} to lie in the local ring at all.
children.approach: Dependency edge only: duplicates the proved sibling longroot-twisted-collapse so the boundary rule sees this node's reliance on it.

children.statement: GAP nonvanishing, CLOSED ON THE MINIMAL STRATUM, conditionally. THEOREM: let nu be MINIMAL in Motegi's order among S(a,b) = {kappa >= lambda, kappa >= mu : {a,b} subset kappa, kappa\{a,b} >= lambda and >= mu}, and nu' = nu\{a,b}. IF Atilde_{nu',lam}|_H and Atilde_{nu',mu}|_H are both nonzero (= nonvanH-localised) THEN ord_H c^nu = -1 exactly, with Res = rho(rho-1) Atilde_{nu',lam}|_H Atilde_{nu',mu}|_H / [t^{-1} Atilde_{nu,nu}]|_H. The argument is complete: minimality + exact-pole-divisor-easy-direction kill propagation (ord_H c^kappa >= 0 for every kappa < nu), the collapse rewrites each Atilde_{nu,X} as rho Atilde_{nu',X} + t u, and the kappa-sum then REASSEMBLES eq:star at the smaller point nu' -- collapsing to a SINGLE term before any cancellation can occur -- leaving rho(rho-1) Atilde_{nu',lam} Atilde_{nu',mu} + tE. Graded 'computed' and not 'proved' ONLY because its one remaining input, nonvanH-localised, is measured and not proved; the boundary rule is doing its job here and I am not promoting a measurement. Verified: 1/1 at N=2 and 19/19 at N=3, ord_H = -1 in all, three pre-registered plants in two blocks (rho(rho-1) -> rho(rho-1)(1+q): fires 19/19; -> rho^2: fires 19/19; Atilde_{nu',mu} -> Atilde_{nu',lam}: fires 10/10 where lam != mu, informatively spared on the 9 where lam = mu).
children.approach: Choose nu minimal so that Theorem C removes every propagated pole, then use the twisted collapse to make the kappa-sum reassemble the defining relation at the deleted point.

children.statement: GAP nonvanH. ord_{H_ab} Atilde_{M,I} = 0 whenever M >= I and {a,b} cap M = empty. This is the LOCALISATION AT H of the converse of Motegi's triangularity (M >= I => Atilde_{M,I} != 0), which Q484 carries as measured 84/84 and not proved -- and it is NOT implied by that converse, since a nonzero Laurent polynomial may still be divisible by w_a w_b - 1. So it is a genuinely separate hypothesis. By longroot-twisted-collapse the case {a,b} subset M reduces to this one, so the single statement is the whole of what is needed; and in the equal-cardinality case |M| = |I| the branching sum has ONE term, reducing it further to non-vanishing of the TYPE A weight function W_{N,r}(w_M|w|I) on a divisor that is not of type A form. MEASURED at N=3 type C: 12/12 on {a,b} cap M = empty, 52/52 on |cap| = 1, with a DISCRIMINATING positive control on {a,b} subset M -- there the prediction ord_H = 0 iff M\{a,b} >= I agrees 41/41 and the control's domain contains BOTH values (12 zeros, 29 positives), so the scan is demonstrably able to detect a violation.
children.approach: Measure ord_H over the three domains separately (cap empty / cap one / cap two) and use the third as a positive control via the sharpness of Lemma A.

children.statement: GAP propagation, the residual gap and the BULK of the problem. For nu NOT minimal in S(a,b), the residue recursion of longroot-poles-simple gives gamma_nu [t^{-1} Atilde_{nu,nu}]|_H = rho(rho-1) Atilde_{nu',lam}|_H Atilde_{nu',mu}|_H - sum_{kappa < nu} gamma_kappa u_{nu,kappa}|_H, and what is unproved is exactly that the two terms on the right do not cancel. This is a strict improvement on the old formulation ('absence of conspiratorial cancellation among the surviving K-terms'): the quantity that must not vanish is written down, the sum is over structure constants rather than branch terms, and the only new analytic object is the first-order collapse deviation u_{nu,kappa}|_H. SCOPE, stated honestly: the minimal stratum covers the jump>=2 triples 1/1, 12/13, 99/127, 690/1136, 4335/9748 at N = 2,3,4,5,6 -- i.e. 100%, 92.3%, 78.0%, 60.7%, 44.5%: COVERAGE DECREASES WITH N. Reporting only the N<=3 figures would have read as a closure. At N=3, 19 of the 25 pole records are created (minimal) and 6 are propagated; the single uncovered triple is (empty,empty,{1,2,3}).
children.approach: Compute the first-order collapse deviation u_{nu,kappa}|_H from the branching formula and look for a grading (q-adic, or cardinality) in which the inhomogeneous term and the propagated sum cannot cancel.
